p.src: Now Xue Ke was still beset by doubts when he suddenly heard a laugh outside the window. He started in alarm and thought, “If it isn't Baochan, it must be Jingui. I shall simply ignore them and see what tricks they have in store.” He listened for a long while, but all was silent again. Nor did he dare touch the wine or fruit. He closed his door and was just about to undress when he heard a faint sound against the paper window. After Baochan's bewildering performance, Xue Ke's heart was in turmoil, and he had no idea what he ought to do. Hearing the paper rustle, he looked closely, but nothing else stirred. Growing suspicious himself, he drew his clothes across his chest and sat before the lamp, lost in thought; then he picked up a piece of fruit and examined it over and over. Suddenly turning his head, he saw that a patch of the window paper was wet. He went over and narrowed his eyes to inspect it, when without warning someone blew through it from outside, giving him a tremendous fright. At the sound of a suppressed giggle, Xue Ke hurriedly blew out the lamp, lay down, and held his breath. Then someone outside said, “Why has Second Master gone to bed without drinking the wine or eating the fruit?” It was unmistakably Baochan's voice again. Xue Ke made no reply and pretended to be asleep. After time enough for another couple of remarks had passed, he heard what sounded like an aggrieved voice outside saying, “How can there be such a hopelessly ill-fated man in all the world?” To Xue Ke it sounded like Baochan's voice and yet also like Jingui's. Only then did he understand what they had been intending. He tossed and turned until after the fifth watch before finally falling asleep. Day had scarcely broken when someone came knocking at his door. Xue Ke hastily asked who it was, but there was no answer from outside. Xue Ke had no choice but to rise and open the door. There stood Baochan, her hair merely gathered together and one hand holding her clothes closed across her breast. She wore a tight little side-fastened jacket edged with patchwork brocade, with a somewhat worn pine-pollen-green sash tied above it. She had put on no skirt, leaving visible her pomegranate-red, flower-sprigged lined trousers and a pair of newly embroidered red shoes. Baochan had not yet washed or dressed her hair; afraid of being seen, she had come early to collect the things. Seeing her dressed this way as she came in, Xue Ke's heart stirred once more. He could only force a smile and ask, “Why are you up so early?” Baochan blushed and said nothing. She merely gathered the fruit onto a plate, picked it up, and left. Seeing her behave so, Xue Ke knew it was because of the previous night and thought, “This is just as well. If they have taken offense and given up the idea altogether, at least they will stop pestering me.” His mind thus eased, he called for someone to bring water so that he could wash his face. He planned to remain quietly at home for a couple of days, partly to compose his mind and partly because, if he went out, he feared those people would come looking for him.

p.src: The fact was that those men who had been friendly with Xue Pan, seeing that there was no one else in the Xue household and that only the still-young Xue Ke was there managing affairs, began to harbor all manner of designs upon him. Some wanted to worm their way in as errand runners; some knew how to draft legal petitions and claimed acquaintance with one or two clerks, offering to smooth matters over at every level; some even urged him to make money on the side while handling the case; and others fabricated rumors to frighten him. Their schemes were of every kind. Whenever Xue Ke saw these people, he kept well away from them. Yet he dared not refuse them to their faces, for fear of provoking some unforeseen trouble. He could only hide at home and await further official word. But no more of this.

p.src: Now Jingui had sent Baochan the previous night to take Xue Ke some wine and fruit and sound out his feelings. On returning, Baochan gave her a full account of his response. Jingui saw that matters had not gone at all smoothly. She feared that all her trouble would come to nothing and that Baochan would look down on her. She wanted to offer a few words to gloss over the affair and change her story, yet she was reluctant to give up such a man, and so, at a loss what to do, she sat there in a daze. Little did she know that Baochan too, aware that Xue Pan was unlikely to return home, was looking for a way forward of her own. But because she feared Jingui might use it against her, she had not dared reveal her intentions. Now that Jingui's actions had already made a beginning, Baochan was only too pleased to trim her sails to the wind. If she could first secure Xue Ke for herself, Jingui would have no choice but to consent; hence she had used her words to egg Jingui on. She had seen that Xue Ke did not seem entirely indifferent, yet neither did he respond very warmly, so for the moment she dared not act rashly. Later, when she saw him blow out the lamp and go to sleep, she was deeply disappointed. She returned and told Jingui, intending to see whether Jingui could devise some means before deciding what to do next. But when she found Jingui sitting there in a daze, apparently at her wits' end, Baochan could only help her prepare for bed, and the two retired. How could Baochan sleep that night? Tossing and turning, she devised a plan: early the next morning she would go first to collect the things, changing into one or two alluring garments but leaving her hair and face unprepared, thereby making herself appear all the more seductive. She would observe Xue Ke's expression while pretending, for her part, to be offended, and would resolutely ignore him. If Xue Ke felt any regret, he would naturally steer his boat toward her shore, and she need not fear that she would fail to secure him first. Yet when she saw Xue Ke, he behaved just as he had the previous night and showed no improper inclination. She therefore had to make her feigned anger real and carry the plate away, though she deliberately left the wine pot behind as a pretext for coming back and renewing the encounter. Jingui asked her, “Did anyone see you when you went to fetch the things?” “No,” replied Baochan. “And Second Master didn't ask you anything?” “No, he didn't,” said Baochan. Jingui had not slept all night and had been unable to devise any plan. Now she could only reconsider the matter: “If I am to do this, I may be able to keep it from others, but how can I hide it from Baochan? I might as well share the benefit with her; then she will naturally spare no effort on my behalf. I cannot go myself and will inevitably need her to act as my intermediary, so I had better consult her and work out a reliable plan.” So she asked with a smile, “What sort of man do you really think Second Master is?” “He seems rather a fool,” replied Baochan. Jingui laughed when she heard this. “How dare you speak of a master that way?” Baochan laughed too. “He has disappointed you, ma'am, so I have every right to say it of him.” “How has he disappointed me? Tell me that,” said Jingui. Baochan replied, “You gave him good things to eat, ma'am, but he would not touch them. Isn't that disappointing your kind intentions?”

p.src: As she spoke, she glanced sidelong at Jingui and smiled. Jingui said, “Don’t let your imagination run wild. I send him things and spare no effort for the master’s sake; that is why I respect him. I asked you only because I was afraid people might spread idle gossip. I don’t understand what you mean by saying such things to me.” Baochan laughed. “Madam, don’t take it amiss. I belong to you—could I possibly harbor divided loyalties? But the matter must be kept secret. If word gets out, it will be no laughing matter.” Jingui felt her face flush and said, “You wretched girl, you’re no decent creature! I suppose you have taken a fancy to him yourself and are merely using me as your pretext—isn’t that it?” Baochan replied, “That is only what you imagine, Madam. I am the one who feels sorry for you. If you truly find the Second Master desirable, I have an idea. Just think, Madam: what mouse does not steal oil? He is merely afraid the affair will not remain secret and that a public scandal would make everyone look disgraceful. In my view, you should not be impatient. For now, keep seeing to whatever he lacks or has overlooked. He is your husband’s younger cousin and has no wife yet. If you show him a little extra care and win his affection, no one can find fault with it. After a few days, when he appreciates your kindness, he will naturally come to thank you. Then prepare some refreshments in our room, and I will help you get him drunk. How could he escape us? If he refuses, we shall simply raise an outcry and accuse him of molesting you. Once frightened, he will naturally have to do as we wish. If he still refuses, he is no man at all, and at least we shall not have lost face for nothing. What do you think, Madam?” At these words Jingui’s cheeks were already glowing red. She laughingly scolded, “You little hussy! You talk as if you had seduced any number of men. No wonder the master could never do without you when he was home.” Baochan curled her lip and said with a laugh, “Oh, enough! Here I am acting as your go-between, Madam, and you turn around and say such things about me.” From then on, Jingui devoted herself to winning Xue Ke over and had no inclination to make trouble. The household consequently enjoyed a little more peace.

p.src: That day Baochan went to fetch the wine pot herself, still wearing her composed, thoroughly proper expression. Stealing a glance at her, Xue Ke instead began to regret his suspicions, wondering whether he might have misjudged the women after all. If so, he had repaid her kindness badly; she might even quarrel with him one day, and would that not be trouble of his own making? The next two days passed in remarkable quiet. Whenever Xue Ke met Baochan, she lowered her head and walked past without even raising her eyes; whenever he met Jingui, however, she rushed warmly toward him like a blaze of fire. Seeing matters thus, Xue Ke actually felt rather ashamed of himself. But we shall leave this aside for now.

p.src: Now Baochai and her mother noticed that Jingui had been quiet for several days and had suddenly grown warm toward everyone; the whole household considered it an extraordinary occurrence. Aunt Xue was delighted. She supposed that when Xue Pan married this woman, they must somehow have offended an unlucky influence, which had brought ruin upon them for all these years. Now that such grave trouble had arisen, only the family’s wealth and the Jia household’s efforts had given them any hope. Since her daughter-in-law had suddenly become peaceable, perhaps Pan’s luck had turned at last. She therefore regarded it privately as a rare wonder. After the meal that day, she came leaning on Tonggui’s arm to visit Jingui’s room. Upon entering the courtyard, she heard a man talking with Jingui. Tonggui, quickly grasping the situation, called out, “Mistress, the old mistress is coming.” As she spoke, they had already reached the doorway. A figure suddenly ducked behind the bedroom door. Startled, Aunt Xue stepped back outside. Jingui said, “Please come inside and sit down, Mother. He is no stranger, only my adoptive brother. He lives in the village and is unaccustomed to meeting people; besides, he has never met you before. He arrived only today and has not yet gone to pay his respects to you.” Aunt Xue said, “If he is your brother, there is no harm in meeting him.” Jingui called her brother out. He bowed to Aunt Xue and offered his greetings. Aunt Xue returned his greeting, sat down, and began conversing with him. Aunt Xue asked, “When did you arrive in the capital?” The man, Xia San, replied, “Last month my mother had no one to manage her household, so she adopted me as her son. I reached the capital only the day before yesterday and came to see my sister today.” Aunt Xue found the fellow unsavory. After sitting only a short while, she rose and said, “Please remain seated.” Turning to Jingui, she added, “As your brother has only just arrived, keep him here for a meal before he leaves.” Jingui assented, and Aunt Xue left. Once her mother-in-law was gone, Jingui said to Xia San, “Stay seated. Now that you have appeared openly today, our Second Master will no longer investigate you. I want you to buy me a few more things today, but do not let anyone see you.” Xia San said, “Just leave that to me. Whatever you want, provided there is money, I can procure it.” Jingui said, “Don’t boast yet. If you buy the wrong thing, I won’t accept it.” They laughed together for a while. Jingui then kept Xia San for supper, told him what to buy, and repeated her instructions before he departed. From then on, Xia San came and went without cease. Though an elderly gatekeeper was on duty, he knew the visitor as the mistress’s brother and seldom reported his visits. This eventually gave rise to endless trouble, but that belongs to a later part of the story. We shall say no more of it now.

u.src: One day a letter arrived from Xue Pan. Aunt Xue opened it and asked Baochai to read it. It said:

p.src: Your son suffers no hardship here in the county jail, so Mother need not worry. But yesterday a clerk at the county yamen said that the prefecture had approved the county’s report, so I thought our influence had taken effect. Who could have known that when the prefecture submitted its report, the circuit authorities would reject and return it? Fortunately, the county’s legal secretary is well disposed toward me and immediately drafted a reply refuting the objection and sent it up. The circuit authorities, however, reprimanded the magistrate. Now the circuit authorities intend to summon me for examination in person. If I am sent up there, I shall suffer again. We must have failed to reach anyone at the circuit yamen. As soon as Mother reads this, please have someone intercede with His Excellency the Intendant without delay. And tell my brother to come quickly, or else I shall be transferred to the circuit yamen. There must be no shortage of silver. Make haste! Make haste!

p.src: When Aunt Xue heard this, she wept all over again, as may well be imagined. Xue Ke consoled her and said, “There is no time to lose.” Having no other recourse, Aunt Xue told Xue Ke to go to the county town and attend to matters. She ordered the servants to pack his luggage at once and change money for him. The family servant Li Xiang was already there looking after things, and Xue Ke set out that very night with another trusted assistant from the shop.

p.src: In the ensuing bustle and confusion, although the servants were handling the preparations, Baochai feared they might overlook something and came to help in person; the commotion continued until the fourth watch before she could rest. After all, she was a delicately reared daughter of a wealthy family; distressed in mind and exhausted by the exertion, she developed a fever that night. By the next day, she could not even take broth or water. Ying’er went to inform Aunt Xue. When Aunt Xue hurried over, she found Baochai’s face crimson and her body burning as though scorched, while she could not utter a word. Aunt Xue was beside herself and wept as though her heart would break. Baoqin supported her and tried to console her. Qiuling too shed floods of tears and kept calling out to Baochai. Baochai could neither speak nor move her hands; her eyes were parched and her nose blocked. A physician was summoned to treat her, and gradually she regained consciousness. Only then did Aunt Xue and the others feel somewhat relieved. By then everyone in both the Rong and Ning mansions had been alarmed. Xifeng first sent someone with Ten-Fragrance Soul-Restoring Pills, and Lady Wang subsequently sent Most-Precious Pills. Grandmother Jia, Ladies Xing and Wang, Madam You, and the others all sent maids to inquire after her, but they kept the news from Baoyu. She was treated continuously for seven or eight days without improvement. At last she herself remembered the Cold-Fragrance Pills; only after taking three did she recover. Baoyu learned of it afterward, but since she had already recovered, he did not go to see her.

u.src: By then everyone in both the Rong and Ning mansions had been alarmed. Xifeng first sent someone with Ten-Fragrance Soul-Restoring Pills, and Lady Wang subsequently sent Most-Precious Pills.
Grandmother Jia, Ladies Xing and Wang, Madam You, and the others all sent maids to inquire after her, but they kept the news from Baoyu.
She was treated continuously for seven or eight days without improvement. At last she herself remembered the Cold-Fragrance Pills; only after taking three did she recover.
Baoyu learned of it afterward, but since she had already recovered, he did not go to see her.

p.src: Around that time another letter arrived from Xue Ke. After reading it, Aunt Xue feared Baochai would worry and did not let her know of it. She herself went to seek Lady Wang’s help and also told her about Baochai’s illness. After Aunt Xue left, Lady Wang in turn appealed to Jia Zheng. Jia Zheng said, “We may rely on those above, but it is hard to rely on those below. We must make the proper arrangements and payments.” Lady Wang then brought up Baochai and said, “The poor child has suffered too. Since she is to become one of our family, we ought to marry her into the household sooner and not let her ruin her health.” Jia Zheng said, “I have been thinking the same. But her family is in turmoil, and now that we have reached the end of winter and the New Year is pressing close, both households naturally have domestic affairs to attend to. For now, let us formalize the betrothal this winter, exchange the ceremonial gifts next spring, and choose a wedding day after the Old Lady’s birthday. Tell Aunt Xue this for the time being.” Lady Wang agreed. The next day, Lady Wang repeated Jia Zheng’s words to Aunt Xue. Aunt Xue reflected that this was reasonable. After the meal, Lady Wang accompanied her to Grandmother Jia’s apartments, where everyone invited them to sit. Grandmother Jia asked, “Have you only just come over, my dear?” Aunt Xue replied, “I actually came yesterday. It was late, however, so I had no chance to come and pay my respects to you.” Lady Wang then repeated to Grandmother Jia everything Jia Zheng had said the previous night, and the old lady was delighted. As they were speaking, Baoyu came in. Grandmother Jia asked him, “Have you eaten?” Baoyu replied, “I have only just returned from school. I am going back after I eat, but I came to see you first, Grandmother. Then I heard that Aunt Xue was here, so I came to pay my respects to her as well.” Then he asked, “Is Cousin Bao much better now?” Aunt Xue smiled and said, “She is well again.” In fact, they had been discussing the marriage just then, but all fell silent when they saw Baoyu enter. Baoyu sat for a while and noticed that Aunt Xue’s manner was not as affectionate as before. He thought, “Even if she is in no mood just now, that is no reason for everyone to stop speaking.” His mind full of suspicions, he went off to school by himself.

p.src: When he returned that evening and had paid his respects to everyone, he went to the Naiad’s House. He lifted the curtain and entered, and Zijuan came to meet him. Seeing no one in the inner room, Baoyu asked, “Where has your young mistress gone?” Zijuan replied, “She went to the main house. When she learned that Aunt Xue had come, she went to pay her respects. Didn’t you go to the main house, Second Master?” Baoyu said, “I have just come from there, but I did not see your young mistress.” “That is strange,” said Zijuan. Baoyu asked, “Then where exactly has she gone?” “I cannot be sure,” Zijuan replied. Baoyu turned and started outside. He had just stepped through the door when he saw Daiyu approaching gracefully with Xueyan. “You are back, Cousin,” said Baoyu. Drawing himself aside, he stepped backward into the room.

Didn’t you go to the main house, Second Master?”
Baoyu said, “I have just come from there, but I did not see your young mistress.”

Baoyu turned and started outside.
He had just stepped through the door when he saw Daiyu approaching gracefully with Xueyan.
“You are back, Cousin,” said Baoyu.
Drawing himself aside, he stepped backward into the room.

p.src: Daiyu came in, passed into the inner room, and invited Baoyu to sit inside. Zijuan brought her an outer garment to change into. After sitting down, Daiyu asked, “Did you see Aunt when you went up there?” “I did,” said Baoyu. Daiyu asked, “Did Aunt mention me?” Baoyu replied, “Not only did she never mention you, but she was not nearly as affectionate toward me as she used to be. When I asked about Cousin Bao’s illness today, she merely smiled and gave me no answer. Can she be blaming me for not visiting Cousin Bao these past two days?” Daiyu smiled and asked, “Have you been to see her?” Baoyu replied, “I did not know about it several days ago. I have known these past two days, but I still haven’t gone.” “There you are,” said Daiyu. Baoyu said, “Grandmother has not told me to go, Mother has not told me to go, and Father has not told me to go either. How would I dare? If that little gate were still passable as it was before, it would be no hardship for me to visit her ten times a day. Now that the gate has been blocked, I must go around by the front, which is naturally inconvenient.” Daiyu said, “How could she know that was the reason?” “Cousin Bao is always most understanding toward me,” said Baoyu. Daiyu said, “Do not deceive yourself. As for Cousin Bao, she has even less reason to be understanding. It is not Aunt who is ill, but Cousin Bao herself. In the old days in the Garden, you composed poems, admired flowers, and drank wine together—what lively times those were! Now that you are separated from them, you see that trouble has befallen her family and that she is seriously ill, yet you behave as if nothing were wrong. How could she not be angry?” Baoyu asked, “Do you mean that Cousin Bao will no longer be friends with me because of this?” Daiyu replied, “Whether she will be friendly with you or not, I cannot say. I am merely reasoning from what is proper.” On hearing this, Baoyu stared blankly for a long while. Seeing him in this state, Daiyu paid him no further heed. She merely ordered someone to replenish the incense, then took out a book and read attentively for a while. Presently Baoyu knitted his brows, stamped his foot, and cried, “Why was a creature like me ever born? The world would be cleaner without me!” Daiyu said, “Indeed, once there is a self, there are others; once there are others, countless vexations arise—fear, delusion, vain dreams, and a host of entanglements and hindrances besides. But everything I said just now was only teasing. You merely saw Aunt looking dispirited; why did you immediately suspect that Cousin Bao was to blame? Aunt came here already distressed over the lawsuit involving her family; how could she have had the spirits to entertain you? It is all because you let your thoughts run wild and strayed into the realm of demons.” Baoyu suddenly saw the light and laughed. “Quite right, quite right.

p.src: Your spiritual understanding is far superior to mine. No wonder that when I lost my temper the year before last and you spoke a few words of Zen to me, I truly could not answer you. Though I may possess a sixteen-foot golden body, I still owe my transformation to a single stalk of yours.” Seizing the opportunity, Daiyu said, “Then let me ask you one question. How will you answer?” Baoyu crossed his legs, pressed his palms together, closed his eyes, pursed his lips, and said, “Ask away.” Daiyu said, “What will you do if Cousin Bao is fond of you? What will you do if Cousin Bao is not fond of you? What will you do if Cousin Bao was fond of you before but is no longer fond of you now? What will you do if she is fond of you today but ceases to be fond of you later? What will you do if you are fond of her but she insists on not being fond of you? And what will you do if you do not wish to be fond of her but she insists on being fond of you?” Baoyu was dumbfounded for a long while, then suddenly burst out laughing. “Though there be three thousand leagues of deep waters, I take but one dipperful to drink.” Daiyu asked, “But what if the dipper floats away upon the water?” Baoyu replied, “It is not the dipper that floats upon the water. The water flows of itself, and the dipper drifts of itself!” Daiyu asked, “But what if the water ceases to flow and the pearl sinks?” Baoyu replied, “My Zen heart is already willow floss mired in mud; do not bid the partridge dance in the spring wind.” Daiyu said, “The first precept of Zen is never to speak falsely.” Baoyu replied, “The Three Treasures are my witness.” Daiyu lowered her head and said nothing. Just then, a crow cawed several times beyond the eaves and flew away toward the southeast. Baoyu said, “I wonder whether that portends good or ill.” Daiyu said, “The good and ill that befall people are not foretold by the cries of birds.” Suddenly Qiuwen came in and said, “Second Master, please go back. Master sent someone into the Garden to ask whether you had returned from school. Sister Xiren could only say that you had already returned. Please hurry!” Baoyu was so frightened that he sprang to his feet and hurried out, while Daiyu did not dare detain him. What the matter was will be revealed in the next chapter.
